Acme and GDPR: What you need to know

Acme has implemented measures to meet its obligations as a Data Processor under the GDPR. We maintain a robust data protection framework that includes:

  • Data Processing Agreement (DPA): Our DPA governs how we process Customer Personal Data in line with GDPR obligations.
  • Security and Safeguards: We implement comprehensive technical and organisational measures (TOMs), along with supplementary protections, to ensure data security and integrity.
  • Data Subject Rights: Acme provides tools to help customers manage GDPR data requests (DSARs).
  • Sub-processors: Acme requires all sub-processors to meet data protection standards equivalent to those in our Customer DPA.
  • International Transfers: Acme is certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (DPF) and also includes the Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) in our DPA to support lawful global data transfers.

We also continuously monitor global privacy regulations to ensure we stay compliant and keep your customers’ data protected.

While Acme meets its GDPR obligations as a Data Processor, each business is responsible for its own compliance as a Data Controller.

While Acme provides a range of tools to help you meet your obligations under the GDPR, compliance ultimately depends on how your business collects, manages, and uses customer data.

Acme supports this through:

  • Storing and processing customer data on your behalf and in accordance with your instructions.
  • Giving you tools to support GDPR compliance.

As the data controller, you are responsible for obtaining valid consent, maintaining accurate records, and responding to individual rights requests.

Acme stores customer data securely using industry-leading encryption and privacy-by-design principles. Data is hosted in an Amazon Web Services (AWS) data center in the United States, which meets strict global compliance and security standards.

Yes. The rules for transferring personal data outside the EU remain the same. Data can be sent abroad if it’s properly protected, via an adequacy decision or an appropriate transfer mechanism.

Acme has self-certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (“DPF”), the UK Extension to the EU-U.S. DPF, and the Swiss-US Data Privacy Framework. Acme’s DPA also incorporates the latest version of the European Commission’s approved Standard Contractual Clauses (“SCCs”). Both the DPF and the SCCs are transfer mechanisms approved under the GDPR.

While GDPR doesn’t require double opt-in, it’s widely recognised as a best practice for maintaining compliance and improving list quality. This method adds an extra verification step, confirming that each subscriber genuinely wants to receive marketing emails or SMS and that their contact details are valid.

With Acme, enabling double opt-in takes just one click. You’ll grow an engaged audience while Acme automatically stores proof of consent and confirmation timestamps for every subscriber—so you always have the transparency and records you need.

Non-compliance can result in penalties up to €20 million or 4% of your annual global revenue, plus reputational damage and loss of customer trust.
